messages:
lee: observed a sharp host-side P99 jump during the streaming harness at 11:08 — from ~180ms to ~700ms. traces point to parsing/tokenize stalls.
nora: is this canary or prod? did anything land recently?
lee: canary. nothing huge in app code but config flips: proxy coalesce disabled, and kernel-selector feature-flag A toggled.
raj: confirmed from perf trace: long wait in parse_loop -> request_tokenizer -> workqueue.wait. tokenizers exhausted.
jen: stack sample shows kernel selector flipped to "mini-batch" path around the same time; that increases parallelism and causes more tokenizer handoffs.
lee: we also saw a lot of very small grpc frames (20-200 bytes) which amplifies syscall/parse overhead. writev disabled meant more syscalls.
karim: KV cache hit rate steady; not a model-side regression. it's purely host ingress/parse.
ops-bot: deploy canary/rls-2026-03-21 completed at 11:00 UTC
nora: quick mitigations?
jen: options: 1) revert kernel-selector flip, 2) bump tokenizer workers, 3) re-enable proxy writev coalesce, 4) add kernel-selector guard for small-frame-heavy bursts.
raj: I pushed a lightweight probe to prefer slim single-token kernel when avg_frame_size < 300 and concurrent_tokenizers_left < 2. it's in a draft PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/hosts/pulls/998
lee: nice. I'll flip writev coalesce on the canary proxy to remove syscall noise.
karim: also consider tokenizer affinity: pin tokenizers to fewer threads to reduce mutex churn. cheap experiment before increasing count.
jen: true but affinity risks uneven load; bumping 4->10 temporarily on canary is quick and low risk.
nora: bump it and watch queue depth and cpu. set a grafana alert for tokenizer_queue_depth > 4 for 2m.
ops-bot: alert rule created: tokenizer_queue_depth > 4 for 2m (owner: eng-runtime)
lee: rolling tokenizer pool up 4->10 on canary now. will post summary in 6m.
raj: thanks — I'm also adding a metric for kernel-selector decisions so we can correlate flips with frame-size distribution.
jen: ran a short local microbench: disabling writev coalesce added ~30% syscall overhead per request for small frames. re-enable should help a lot.
karim: follow-ups: raj open selector-guard PR, nora observe canary after pool bump, lee flip proxy coalesce, jen validate memory + CPU after coalesce.
lee: good call. documenting incident note: https://docs/internal/ingress-spike-2026-03-21. will update after metrics.
